History:
• Presenting complaint: Persistent dry cough & runny nose for 5–6 days  
• Course: Continuous dry cough, worse at night, causing sleep disturbance; rhinorrhea started simultaneously  
• Associated symptoms: Chills/shivering (subjective fever, temperature not taken); fatigue & generalized myalgias (arms & legs); transient diarrhea at onset (resolved); mild throat irritation from coughing only  
• Negatives: No productive sputum, chest pain, dyspnea on routine activity, ear pain/discharge, nausea/vomiting, rash, urinary symptoms  
• Exposures: Partner asymptomatic; no unusual work stress; quit smoking 6 mo ago

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus  
• Hypertension  
Allergies: Denies drug allergies  
Medications:  
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented  
Family history: Father – type 2 diabetes  
Social: Lives with partner; IT developer; ex-smoker (quit 6 mo); alcohol 2–3 glasses wine on ~3 nights/week

Physical Examination:
(Remote consult – no formal exam)  
• Patient alert, conversant; dry cough audible over phone  
• No reported breathlessness at rest or on exertion  
• No chest pain, ear findings, or visible rash (by history)

Impression:
Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection (self-limiting)

Management Plan:
• Supportive care: rest, maintain hydration, regular Paracetamol for fever/myalgia  
• Advise 1–2 days off work to recuperate and reduce transmission risk  
• Safety-netting: return in 2–3 days if no improvement, sooner if breathing worsens, fever persists, or cough > 1 week—consider chest exam and possible antibiotics  
• Lifestyle: Gradual reduction of alcohol intake (target ≤2 glasses/week initially) for BP/diabetes benefit  
• Routine diabetes & hypertension follow-up with usual physician unchanged

Patient Summary:
50-year-old woman with diabetes & hypertension presents with 5-day history of dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, and fatigue. Features and time course suggest uncomplicated viral URI; no red-flag respiratory symptoms. Provided supportive measures and clear return precautions.

Key Takeaways:
1. Rest and drink plenty of fluids; use Paracetamol as needed.  
2. Stay home for a couple of days; resume work when symptoms improve.  
3. Seek review if breathing gets harder, fever or cough persist > 2–3 days, or any new concerns arise.

Next Steps:
• Monitor symptoms over next 48–72 hrs  
• Re-consult if not improving or worsening; may require physical exam, vitals, and chest assessment ± antibiotics  
• Continue routine chronic-disease monitoring; consider alcohol reduction plan
